journal.text: Initiated a diversified momentum portfolio, investing $48,000 and retaining about $2,000 cash. APP is the strongest software/AI trend; STX, MU, and LRCX provide exposure to strong storage, memory, and semiconductor-equipment trends; TSLA has sustained a powerful September breakout; XEL adds a lower-volatility utility breakout and reduces pure tech concentration. As of 2025-09-30, all six were materially above late-August levels and near recent highs, with APP 718.54, STX 236.06, MU 167.32, LRCX 133.90, TSLA 444.72, and XEL 80.65. Reconsider or trim if trends fail: roughly APP below 640, STX below 217, MU below 156, LRCX below 126, TSLA below 420, or XEL below 77; rotate toward stronger eligible names rather than averaging down. Keep cash reserve for gaps and future deployment.

Held the six-position momentum portfolio and retained $2,000 cash. The first post-entry close broadly confirmed the allocation: STX 256.84, MU 182.15, LRCX 142.79, and TSLA 459.46 advanced strongly; APP at 704.09 remains well above its risk level, while XEL at 80.31 continues to provide defensive diversification. No thesis breach justifies turnover after one session, and adding after sharp one-day semiconductor gains would reduce flexibility. Reconsider on sustained closes near the existing trend-failure levels—APP 640, STX 217, MU 156, LRCX 126, TSLA 420, XEL 77—or if materially stronger relative momentum emerges elsewhere.

Held all six positions and the $2,005 cash reserve. Semiconductor/storage momentum remains exceptionally strong: MU closed 183.75, LRCX 146.99, and STX 254.74, all near recent highs after major advances. APP’s second pullback close at 683.64 remains above its breakout/support area, while XEL at 79.60 still holds its late-September utility breakout. TSLA’s high-volume reversal from a 470.75 intraday high to 436 is the main risk signal, but it remains above the 420 support/risk level, so one reversal does not yet warrant selling. No alternative reviewed offered enough improvement to justify turnover or greater semiconductor concentration. Reconsider APP below roughly 650, STX below 235, MU below 168, LRCX below 134, TSLA on a close below 420, and XEL below 77; also reconsider if TSLA cannot stabilize after this reversal.

Exited TSLA and rotated $7,500 into INSM, retaining the other five positions and roughly the existing cash reserve. TSLA failed to stabilize after Thursday’s high-volume reversal: Friday produced another lower close at 429.83, a lower intraday low of 416.58, and elevated volume, weakening the breakout despite recovering above 420. INSM offers sector diversification and cleaner relative momentum, rising from 137.03 on September 26 to 157.16 on October 3 and breaking above its prior 149 area on expanding volume. APP, STX, MU, and LRCX remain above their trend-risk levels; XEL still holds its utility breakout. Reconsider INSM on a close below roughly 145; APP below 650, STX below 235, MU below 168, LRCX below 134, and XEL below 77. Re-enter TSLA only after clear stabilization and renewed strength rather than averaging into the reversal.

Exited APP after its thesis decisively failed: it plunged from 682.76 to 587, traded as low as 545, and volume expanded to 14.4 million, breaking well below the 650 risk level. Reallocated the proceeds equally to DASH and MSFT rather than increasing the already-large semiconductor exposure. DASH closed at a 30-session high of 281.74 on stronger volume after clearing its prior 275 area; MSFT also reached a 30-session closing high at 528.57 after breaking above its recent 520-521 ceiling. Held STX despite its pullback because 242.83 remains above the 235 risk level; MU, LRCX, INSM, and XEL remain above their stated trend levels. Reconsider DASH below roughly 265, MSFT below 510, STX below 235, MU below 168, LRCX below 134, INSM below 145, and XEL below 77.

Exited STX after its trend thesis failed: it closed at 225.01, below the stated 235 risk level, following a second sharp decline; Tuesday's drop reached 223 and volume surged to 10.0 million, roughly double the prior session. Rotated only $5,000 into AEP and retained the rest as cash because semiconductor volatility has risen. AEP provides defensive diversification and clean relative momentum, advancing from 107.05 on September 22 to a 30-session high of 118.16, with the latest session closing near its high. Held MU and LRCX because they remain above their 168 and 134 risk levels despite Tuesday's pullback. INSM and XEL continued to new highs, while DASH and MSFT remain above 265 and 510. Reconsider AEP below roughly 112, MU below 168, LRCX below 134, INSM below 145, XEL below 77, DASH below 265, and MSFT below 510.

Added a $3,000 starter position in DDOG while retaining roughly $2,300 cash and all seven existing holdings. DDOG broke to a 30-session high at 164.12 on 7.5 million shares, versus 154.52 the prior session and materially above its recent volume, extending the constructive sequence from 139.07 on September 26. The starter size limits gap risk and diversifies away from the large semiconductor allocation. MU rebounded to a new closing high at 196.54, while LRCX recovered to 142.54; both remain above their risk levels. INSM, XEL, DASH, MSFT, and AEP also remain above thesis-invalidating levels. Reconsider DDOG on a close below roughly 151; AEP below 112, MU below 168, LRCX below 134, INSM below 145, XEL below 77, DASH below 265, and MSFT below 510.

Held the eight positions and $2,288.59 cash. No thesis-invalidating level was breached: MU closed 192.33, LRCX 141.00, INSM 164.40, XEL 81.26, DASH 275.44, MSFT 522.40, AEP 116.91, and DDOG 164.07. DDOG consolidated its high-volume breakout with a tight session and INSM made another 30-session closing high. MU and LRCX remain strong but volatile, so retaining cash is preferable to adding more semiconductor exposure. AEP, XEL, DASH, and MSFT pulled back without breaking support. Fresh strength in CEG, ARM, and NVDA is notable, but with the account already 95% invested I will not chase another position after yesterday's DDOG addition. Reconsider on closes below roughly DDOG 151, AEP 112, MU 168, LRCX 134, INSM 145, XEL 77, DASH 265, or MSFT 510; consider deploying cash if CEG or another leader holds a breakout while an existing holding weakens.

Exited the full LRCX position after its trend thesis failed. It closed at 131.37, below the previously stated 134 risk level, after falling from 141.00; Friday's 18.75 million-share volume was the highest of the last 30 sessions and the close was near the 131.02 low. I am not immediately rotating the proceeds because Friday produced broad, high-volume weakness across growth and semiconductor leaders. Held MU because 181.60 remains above its 168 risk level, and held DDOG, DASH, MSFT, INSM, XEL, and AEP because their closes remain above the stated levels, though DASH at 266.02 and MSFT at 510.96 are now marginal. Reconsider on closes below roughly MU 168, DDOG 151, DASH 265, MSFT 510, INSM 145, XEL 77, or AEP 112. Keep the increased cash reserve until the market stabilizes or a leader establishes fresh relative strength.

Added a $3,000 starter position in ARM while retaining roughly $7,600 cash and all existing holdings. ARM reversed Friday's broad selloff with an 11.1% gain to 171.94, a new 30-session closing high, on 11.19 million shares; it closed near the 175 session high and above the prior 170.66 peak. The modest size recognizes its volatility and the fact that broad stabilization is only one session old. Existing holdings remained above their stated risk levels: MU 192.77, DDOG 164.20, DASH 273.52, MSFT 514.05, INSM 163.94, XEL 80.16, and AEP 116.80. Reconsider ARM on a close below roughly 153; retain prior risk levels of MU 168, DDOG 151, DASH 265, MSFT 510, INSM 145, XEL 77, and AEP 112. Avoid further deployment unless the rebound broadens or leaders sustain fresh highs.

Added a $3,000 starter position in CEG and retained roughly $4,600 cash. CEG closed at 389.56, a new 40-session closing high, after reversing from 366.16 to finish near its 395.14 session high; this confirms the fresh relative strength previously required before deploying more cash. Position size is modest because the session range was wide and broad technology leadership remains uneven. Held all existing positions: MU 187.06, DDOG 160.88, DASH 270.54, MSFT 513.57, INSM 161.38, XEL 80.85, AEP 118.38, and ARM 168.16 all remain above their stated risk levels. Reconsider CEG on a close below roughly 360; retain risk levels near MU 168, DDOG 151, DASH 265, MSFT 510, INSM 145, XEL 77, AEP 112, and ARM 153. Avoid further buying unless leadership broadens or another position is exited.

Held all positions and retained $4,631.77 cash. CEG extended its breakout to 403.95 on rising volume and closed near the 412.70 high, but after two consecutive additions the position is already adequately sized and the stock is too extended to chase. MU, ARM and INSM remain constructive, while XEL and AEP provide steadier leadership. Broad conditions are still uneven: AMD, AMAT, ASML, KLAC and MPWR rebounded, but NVDA weakened again and many software/consumer leaders remain below recent highs. No thesis-based close stop was breached: MU 168, XEL 77, INSM 145, DASH 265, MSFT 510, AEP 112, DDOG 151, ARM 153, and CEG 360. Reconsider any holding on a close below its level; deploy cash only on broader confirmation or a well-controlled fresh breakout rather than chasing CEG.

Exited DDOG and held all other positions. DDOG fell 5.5% to 151.17 on increased volume, closed near the session low after trading down to 149.02, and finished only 0.11% above the stated 151 close-risk level. That high-volume reversal and intraday support failure make the practical thesis weak enough to exit rather than risk a gap through support. DASH also reversed sharply but remains above its 265 close threshold; MSFT remains above 510. MU's high-volume breakout remains strong, while INSM, ARM, XEL, AEP and CEG retain constructive trends. Keep the resulting cash reserve rather than replace DDOG amid uneven breadth. Reconsider remaining holdings on closes below MU 168, XEL 77, INSM 145, DASH 265, MSFT 510, AEP 112, ARM 153, or CEG 360; consider redeploying only after broad confirmation or a controlled breakout.

Exited DASH after its 263.06 close breached the stated 265 risk level. The breach followed Thursday's wide, high-volume reversal; Friday then traded down to 257.71 and failed to recover 265, confirming loss of near-term support rather than a one-day shakeout. Held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM and CEG. MU remains the strongest holding near its highs; INSM and the utilities remain constructive. ARM and CEG pulled back but remain above their risk levels, while MSFT held just above 510. Kept the DASH proceeds in cash because breadth remains uneven and the portfolio already has substantial semiconductor and utility exposure. Reconsider on closes below MU 168, XEL 77, INSM 145, MSFT 510, AEP 112, ARM 153, or CEG 360; redeploy cash only on a controlled breakout or broader confirmation.

Bought $5,000 of AAPL and held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM and CEG. AAPL broke above the prior 259 area to 262.24, closed near its 264.38 high, and did so on 90.5 million shares—roughly double its recent volume—providing the controlled, liquid breakout required before redeploying part of the cash reserve. The position is deliberately moderate because overall breadth remains mixed and the account already carries meaningful technology exposure; about half the opening cash remains uncommitted. MU and INSM remain strong, ARM rebounded, and XEL/AEP remain constructive. CEG's fall to 370 is concerning, but it still closed above the established 360 risk level, so I held rather than preempt the rule. Reconsider AAPL on a close below 252, and existing holdings on closes below MU 168, XEL 77, INSM 145, MSFT 510, AEP 112, ARM 153, or CEG 360.

Exited CEG after its 358.79 close breached the established 360 risk level. The break followed a rapid retreat from 403.95: CEG closed at 370 on Monday, then traded down to 355.20 and finished near the low, confirming that the recent uptrend has failed rather than merely paused. Held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM and AAPL. AAPL's high-volume breakout remains intact above 252; MU is consolidating above 200 after its breakout, INSM and the utilities remain constructive, and MSFT/ARM remain above support. Kept the CEG proceeds in cash rather than chase mixed semiconductor and growth setups after uneven reversals. Reconsider holdings on closes below MU 185, XEL 77, INSM 155, MSFT 510, AEP 112, ARM 153, or AAPL 252; redeploy cash only after another controlled breakout or broader confirmation.

Bought $4,000 of CCEP and held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM and AAPL. CCEP provided the controlled, diversifying breakout required for partial cash deployment: it advanced from 90.54 to 90.78, 91.78 and 92.52 over four sessions, closed near its 92.92 high, and reached a new 30-session closing high while many semiconductor and growth names weakened. The position is moderate because volume was not exceptional and the portfolio retains several near-term risk points. Existing stops remain unbroken, though INSM's retreat to 160.40 and AAPL's pullback from its breakout merit monitoring. Keep remaining cash reserved. Reconsider CCEP on a close below 89.50, and existing holdings on closes below MU 185, XEL 77, INSM 155, MSFT 510, AEP 112, ARM 153, or AAPL 252.

Held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM, AAPL and CCEP, retaining $4,191.69 cash. No closing-risk threshold was breached. MU rebounded from 198.47 to 206.71 and remains the portfolio's strongest trend. AAPL stabilized at 259.58 above its breakout support, while MSFT and ARM held their ranges. XEL and AEP remain constructive despite modest pullbacks. INSM tested 154.79 intraday but recovered to 160.12, so its close-based 155 rule did not trigger. CCEP's first-session reversal from a 93.03 high to 91.29 weakens the breakout but does not justify an immediate exit above 89.50. Avoided deploying the remaining cash after mixed follow-through. Reconsider on closes below MU 185, XEL 77, INSM 155, MSFT 510, AEP 112, ARM 153, AAPL 252, or CCEP 89.50.

Held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM, AAPL and CCEP, retaining $4,191.69 cash. No established close-based risk level was breached. Friday brought broader growth confirmation: MU surged from 206.71 to a new 30-session high of 219.02, while AMD, NVDA, LRCX, KLAC, LITE and CRWD also advanced. I did not chase those extended moves at the next unknown open because the account is already about 92% invested and MU is roughly 21% of net worth. AAPL resumed strength at 262.82, MSFT improved to 523.61, and ARM recovered to 170.68. INSM remains the closest risk point after three closes near 160, while AEP is weakening but still above support; CCEP continues holding its breakout area. Reconsider on closes below MU 198, XEL 77, INSM 155, MSFT 510, AEP 112, ARM 160, AAPL 252, or CCEP 89.50. Deploy cash only on a controlled pullback or a fresh breakout not already extended.

Held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM, AAPL and CCEP, keeping $4,191.69 cash. All positions remain above their close-based risk levels. Monday confirmed broad strength: MU held its breakout at 220.10 after an intraday high of 224.98; AAPL closed at a new 40-session high of 268.81; MSFT gapped higher to 531.52; and ARM advanced 4.7% to 178.62 on increased volume. INSM rebounded to 164.02, easing the immediate support concern. XEL, AEP and CCEP remain stable diversifiers, though AEP's trend is softer and CCEP has not followed through strongly. I did not deploy the final 8% cash because the strongest growth names have risen sharply for multiple sessions and today's open is unknown, while MU already represents about 21% of account value. Reconsider on closes below MU 206, XEL 77, INSM 155, MSFT 510, AEP 112, ARM 165, AAPL 258, or CCEP 89.50; deploy cash only after a controlled pullback or a non-extended breakout.

Held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM, AAPL and CCEP, retaining $4,191.69 cash. No close-based risk level was breached on October 28. MU consolidated its breakout at 221.91 on lighter volume, AAPL held its high at 269.00, and INSM continued recovering to 165.29. MSFT closed at 542.07 after a large gap and elevated volume; ARM pulled back to 173.09 but remains above support. AEP weakened to 115.11 and is the softest holding, yet remains above the 112 exit level. I did not chase fresh strength: NVDA surged 5.0% to 201.03 on nearly 298 million shares, while AVGO and CRWD also reached short-term highs, and the account already has substantial semiconductor exposure through MU and ARM. Reconsider on closes below MU 206, XEL 77, INSM 155, MSFT 523, AEP 112, ARM 165, AAPL 258, or CCEP 89.50. Deploy cash after a controlled pullback or a breakout that is not already extended.

Sold the full CCEP position after its October 29 close fell to 88.62, below the precommitted 89.50 risk level; the 3.6% drop also erased the recent breakout attempt. Held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM and AAPL. AEP reversed its prior weakness with a gap to 120.30 and a 122.11 close on 9.57 million shares, so it remains held rather than sold. MU, AAPL and INSM continued higher, while ARM stayed above 165 support. I am retaining the CCEP proceeds as cash because leading alternatives such as NVDA, AVGO, PLTR and LITE have just made sharp, extended advances, and AMZN remains below its September resistance near 238. Reconsider on closes below MU 215, XEL 77, INSM 159, MSFT 523, AEP 115, ARM 165, or AAPL 262; redeploy cash after a controlled pullback or a confirmed, non-extended breakout.

Held MU, XEL, INSM, MSFT, AEP, ARM and AAPL, retaining $8,023.50 cash. No precommitted close-based exit was breached on October 30. INSM broke sharply higher from 166.95 to 194.22 on 6.73 million shares and closed near its 194.70 high, so I am allowing the high-volume breakout to run rather than immediately trimming. XEL recovered to 81.59 on elevated volume, while AAPL held near its high and MU consolidated at 224.01. MSFT's high-volume drop to 525.76 was concerning but remained above 523 and the prior 523.61 breakout close. ARM is the weakest holding, closing at 165.45 just above its 165 risk level after three declines; I will exit on a close below 165. I did not deploy cash because GOOG, NVDA, AVGO, STX and other leaders are extended or volatile after sharp moves, while AMZN sold off to 222.86 on unusually heavy volume. Reconsider on closes below MU 215, XEL 78, INSM 175, MSFT 523, AEP 115, ARM 165, or AAPL 262; consider new buys only after orderly consolidation or a non-extended breakout.

Sold the full MSFT position after its October 31 close fell to 517.81, below the precommitted 523 risk level, on a second consecutive high-volume decline. Deployed part of the new monthly cash while retaining a meaningful reserve. Bought GOOG and AMZN because both cleared multi-month resistance on exceptional volume after gap moves: GOOG held 281.82 for a second session above the former 275 area, while AMZN closed at 244.22 above its prior resistance near 238 despite an intraday fade. Bought PANW near its 220.24 high after a controlled advance, GILD after it held its large October 28 breakout for three sessions near 652, and a smaller ROST position near a relatively orderly 158.92 breakout to diversify away from semiconductors. Held MU, XEL, INSM, AEP, ARM and AAPL; ARM bounced back above 169, while no other existing close-based risk level was breached. Reconsider on closes below MU 215, XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, ARM 165, AAPL 262, GOOG 268, AMZN 238, PANW 211, GILD 635, or ROST 154. Avoid adding if gap breakouts reverse on heavy volume.

Sold the full GILD position because the prior purchase thesis was based on a ticker/evidence mismatch: the cited breakout near 652 belonged to REGN, while GILD actually traded near 120 and had not produced that breakout. GILD closed at 122.05 for a small gain versus the 119.82 cost, so I corrected the process error rather than rationalizing the holding after the fact. Held all other positions. MU rebounded to 234.70, GOOG held its gap breakout at 284.12, and AMZN followed its earnings gap with a second strong close at 254. PANW and ROST remain above support; INSM is pulling back from its breakout but remains above 175. Retaining the proceeds as cash because many leaders are extended and broad action is mixed. Reconsider on closes below MU 215, XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, ARM 165, AAPL 262, GOOG 275, AMZN 243, PANW 211, or ROST 154. Consider redeployment after an orderly setup rather than chasing PLTR, IDXX, or other sharp advances.

Sold the full ARM position because its November 4 close of 160.73 decisively breached the precommitted 165 risk level, following a gap down and a close near the session low. Held the remaining positions and did not redeploy cash. Broad growth and semiconductor action was weak: MU reversed from 234.70 to 218.03 on increased volume, while NVDA, AVGO, AMD and several other leaders also declined. MU nevertheless remained above its 215 close-based risk level. GOOG held above 275, AMZN remained above its earnings-gap support, and AAPL, XEL, AEP and ROST were comparatively resilient. INSM's post-breakout pullback continued on lower volume and stayed above 175. PANW is close to support but still above 211. Reconsider on closes below MU 215, XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, GOOG 275, AMZN 243, PANW 211, or ROST 154. Keep the enlarged cash reserve until broad selling stabilizes or a strong, non-extended setup emerges.

Bought a $6,000 AMGN position after its November 5 high-volume advance to 319.86 cleared the prior 303-304 resistance area and closed near the session high. The breakout adds non-technology exposure while leaving roughly $20,000 cash because broader growth remains mixed and several leaders are volatile. Held all existing positions: MU rebounded strongly to 237.50 on increased volume after Tuesday's reversal; GOOG recovered to 284.75; AMZN held its earnings-gap area; INSM stabilized above 175; and AAPL, XEL, AEP and ROST remain constructive. PANW weakened to 213.18 but has not yet breached the precommitted 211 close-based risk level. Reconsider AMGN on a close below 302, particularly on heavy volume. Reconsider other positions on closes below MU 215, XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, GOOG 275, AMZN 243, PANW 211, or ROST 154. Avoid chasing LITE or STX after their sharp one-day surges and retain cash unless market breadth improves.

Held all positions and kept $20,218.94 in cash because the November 6 session showed broad growth weakness and no fresh setup justified adding exposure. The two weakest holdings finished directly above their precommitted close-based exits rather than below them: AMZN closed 243.04 versus 243 and PANW 211.37 versus 211. AMZN's close near its 242.17 low and PANW's intraday break to 207.35 warrant no additional tolerance; sell on a subsequent close below those levels. MU remained a relative leader, closing 238.33 after reaching 246.41 on elevated volume; GOOG held its earnings gap at 285.34; INSM stabilized at 185.68; and AMGN's orderly 315.59 pullback preserved the November 5 breakout. AAPL, XEL, AEP, and ROST remain above risk levels. Reconsider on closes below MU 215, XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, GOOG 275, AMZN 243, PANW 211, ROST 154, or AMGN 302. Avoid buying into the current broad selloff unless breadth stabilizes or a strong non-extended breakout appears.

Bought $5,000 of MAR because its November 7 advance closed at 291.16 near the 291.66 high on increased volume, decisively extending the November 5 breakout while most growth stocks remained weak. This adds a relatively strong non-technology position but preserves about $15,264 cash given fragile breadth. Held all existing positions: no close-based exit triggered. AMZN rebounded to 244.41 after testing 238.49, PANW recovered to 212.29 after another intraday support test, GOOG remained above 275, and MU, INSM, AEP, AMGN and the defensive holdings showed relative resilience. Reconsider MAR on a close below 279, which would negate the latest breakout. Other close-based risk levels remain MU 215, XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, GOOG 275, AMZN 243, PANW 211, ROST 154, and AMGN 302. Do not add broadly unless market breadth stabilizes further.

Bought $5,000 of ISRG after its November 10 advance closed at 576.20 near the 578.30 high on rising volume. The move followed November 7's breakout above the roughly 552 ceiling of its post-gap consolidation, and the close remained only about 4.4% above that pivot. This adds a healthcare leader while retaining about $10,264 cash. Held all existing positions because no close-based exit triggered: MU surged to 253.30, GOOG recovered to 290.59, AMZN improved to 248.40, PANW reached 216.54, and AMGN, INSM, AEP and MAR remained constructive. Reconsider ISRG on a close below 548, which would negate the breakout. Raise MU's risk level to 232 and GOOG's to 278; retain close-based levels XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, AMZN 243, PANW 211, ROST 154, AMGN 302, and MAR 279. Avoid further broad additions unless the rebound develops stronger breadth.

Held all positions and retained $10,263.96 cash. No close-based exit triggered: MU's sharp pullback from 253.30 ended at 241.11, still above 232; GOOG held 291.74 above 278; AMZN, PANW, and ISRG remained above 243, 211, and 548. AMGN was the strongest holding, breaking to 338.45 near its session high, while AAPL advanced to 275.25 and INSM continued higher to 193.69. I did not add because breadth remained uneven: MU reversed sharply and several semiconductor leaders weakened, while the portfolio is already about 90% invested across 12 positions. Raise AMGN's close-based risk level to 318, the breakout-gap area. Retain levels MU 232, XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, GOOG 278, AMZN 243, PANW 211, ROST 154, MAR 279, and ISRG 548. Reconsider adding only after broader participation or a strong, non-extended breakout.

Sold the full PANW position after its November 12 close at 210.04 breached the 211 close-based risk level. The exit follows a sharp reversal from 220.03 to near the session low on increased volume, negating the recent rebound and respecting the predefined rule. I did not redeploy the proceeds: breadth remains uneven, with weakness in several growth leaders, while the remaining 11 positions still provide substantial exposure. AMZN closed at 244.20, narrowly above its 243 level, and MU, GOOG, and ISRG remain above 232, 278, and 548. Retain levels XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, ROST 154, AMGN 318, MAR 279, plus the levels above. Reconsider PANW only after a decisive recovery above roughly 220; redeploy cash only into a strong, non-extended breakout with broader participation.

Sold the full AMZN position after its November 13 close at 237.58 decisively breached the 243 close-based risk level. The stock fell from a 243.05 open to near its 236.50 session low on increased volume, breaking the post-earnings support area and invalidating the hold thesis. I retained the other 10 positions because their close-based levels were not breached: MU closed 236.95 above 232 despite a high-volume selloff, GOOG finished 279.12 just above 278, and ISRG held 565.51 above 548. Broad growth and semiconductor weakness—including sharp declines in NVDA, AMAT, AVGO, LITE, PLTR, SHOP, and TSLA—argues against redeploying proceeds, leaving a substantial cash reserve. Retain levels XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, GOOG 278, ROST 154, AMGN 318, MAR 279, ISRG 548, and MU 232. Reconsider AMZN only after a convincing recovery through roughly 245-250; consider new buying only when breadth stabilizes and a leader offers a non-extended breakout.

Sold the full GOOG position after its November 14 close at 276.98 breached the predefined 278 close-based risk level. The stock gapped down to 271.89 and, despite recovering from the session low, remained below the post-earnings support area for the first close since the rule was set. I did not redeploy: broad growth and semiconductor action remains damaged and volatile, while the portfolio retains meaningful exposure and a larger cash reserve is appropriate. ISRG closed 549.51, narrowly above 548, and MU rebounded strongly to 246.83 on heavy volume while holding 232; both remain holds for now. Retain close-based levels XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, ROST 154, AMGN 318, MAR 279, ISRG 548, and MU 232. Reconsider GOOG only after a convincing recovery above roughly 284-292; consider new buying when market breadth stabilizes or a leader offers a controlled, non-extended breakout.

Sold the full ISRG position after its November 17 close at 546.71 breached the predefined 548 close-based risk level. The stock has retreated from 576.20 through several consecutive lower closes and finished below the post-earnings support area, so I am respecting the rule despite the modest size of the breach. I did not redeploy: broad action remains weak, with continued deterioration across software, semiconductors, consumer growth, and transports; GOOG's high-volume rebound to 285.60 was encouraging but closed well off its 294.52 high and has not yet established a convincing recovery through the 284-292 zone. Retain close-based levels MU 232, XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, ROST 154, AMGN 318, and MAR 279. Reconsider ISRG after a sustained recovery above roughly 560-576, and add risk only after broader participation stabilizes or a leader produces a controlled breakout.

Sold the full MU position after its November 18 close at 228.50 breached the predefined 232 close-based risk level. The stock gapped lower, traded down to 225.52, and closed near the low on elevated volume after failing to sustain the November 14 rebound; this invalidates the recent support thesis. I did not redeploy because broad conditions remain weak: semiconductors and software continued lower, while many consumer and transport names are also deteriorating. INSM, AMGN, AEP, XEL, AAPL, ROST, and MAR remain above their close-based levels. Retain levels XEL 78, INSM 175, AEP 115, AAPL 262, ROST 154, AMGN 318, and MAR 279. Reconsider MU only after a convincing recovery above roughly 240-247; add new risk after breadth stabilizes or a leader clears resistance with controlled price action.

Initiated measured positions in GOOG and GILD while retaining a substantial cash reserve. GOOG closed at 292.99 on very heavy volume after trading to 304.25, completing the previously required recovery through roughly 284-292; although the close below the intraday high argues against a full-sized entry, its relative strength and reclaimed post-earnings range justify an $8,000 starter.
